text:
riley: discovered a bug in py-sdk v0.7.3 async client where non-json error bodies get dropped. server returns 401 text/html and the raised RedwoodAPIError has neither status nor the response body attached. callers can't decide retry vs auth-failure. any quick fixes? anika: ugh. can you paste the exception text and a tiny repro? async versus sync? riley: async. repro is basically: ```py async with RedwoodClient(api_key=...) as client: await client.items.list() # upstream returns 401 with HTML error page ``` raised exception snippet: ``` redwood.errors.RedwoodAPIError: unable to parse error payload # no .http_status, no .body or .raw_body ``` headers: `content-type: text/html; charset=UTF-8`, body: `

Unauthorized

` leo: iirc we introduced richer error metadata for sync calls (http_status, raw_bytes, text) but async code path uses a thin wrapper that lost those attrs when re-raising. the fix should be to attach metadata to the exception before re-raising. simon: recommendation: keep internal raw_bytes (Optional[bytes]) and expose public attributes on RedwoodAPIError as `http_status: Optional[int]`, `raw_body: Optional[str]`, `raw_bytes: Optional[bytes]`, and `parsed_json: Optional[dict]`. When content-type is not json, set parsed_json=None, but always populate raw_bytes and attempt to decode to raw_body using resp.charset or utf-8 with errors='replace'. jen: +1. also add `RedwoodAPIError.json()` helper that returns parsed_json or raises a clear MessageParsingError if not present. update the typeshed (.pyi) so mypy users see the attrs. we should avoid changing public attr names if possible to not break consumers. so prefer `raw_body` and `raw_bytes` additions rather than renaming things. ci-bot: CI: branch async-error-metadata — tests failing (mypy: missing attribute on RedwoodAPIError) leo: for backwards compat, if previous exceptions already had `.body` we should keep that alias but mark as deprecated. propose implementing properties: `body` property returns `raw_body` for now and emits a deprecation warning. anika: tests to add: stub-level unit test (mypy) to assert attributes exist, plus runtime unit that mocks aiohttp.Response with content-type text/plain and binary gzipped payload to ensure raw_bytes preserved. include a tiny example in docs under errors.rst describing `except RedwoodAPIError as e: print(e.http_status, e.raw_body, e.raw_bytes)` riley: i can open the PR. target release 0.7.4 as a patch. will include changelog entry and example in docs. simon: small gotcha: some callers compare str(e) to body text — ensure `__str__` falls back to `http_status` + `raw_body` if parsed_json is empty, but avoid leaking huge binary content. maybe truncate to 1000 chars. jen: good point. add a unit that asserts __str__ is truncated for very large bodies. riley: thanks. i'll draft the PR and ping reviewers @leo @anika. leaving a curl example for folks to reproduce locally: `curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer bad" https://api.redwood.com/v1/items` returns `HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized` with an HTML body on our staging proxy. anika: :thumbsup:
